name: Pingarrón hill, Jarama
story: The 695 m Pingarrón dominated the Jarama battlefield and changed hands several times in hand-to-hand fighting. Nationalist troops took it in mid-February; Republican units, including Líster's men and the XV International Brigade, tried repeatedly to retake it. On 27 February the Abraham Lincoln Battalion, about 450 Americans under Robert Merriman, was ordered to attack without the promised artillery and air support and lost well over half its men, among them the Irish poet Charles Donnelly. The Nationalists kept the hill; the battle ended in stalemate, with both armies dug in facing each other until 1939.
see: Ridge-top trenches, stone parapets and nearby Republican positions (Cota 700, Cota 666) with views over the Jarama valley.
plan: Reached on foot by Morata's battle routes 5 and 6 (several km on farm tracks). Morata's route leaflet notes the hill itself is private property with difficult access, so keep to the public tracks. Rough ground: wear boots.

boxes.text: Lincoln Battalion losses on 27 Feb are given variously (e.g. 120 dead and 175 wounded).
